title: What Is This Code Allowed to Change? — Final Video
product_promise: Replace the implementation-level question of whether to read AI-generated code with the authority question: what may this code make true, and who owns the result?

beats.entry_visual: The full question ‘Should we read AI-generated code?’ is readable on the warm porcelain field at frame zero.
beats.visual_reason: The familiar debate is established, struck through, and replaced by the missing distinction between writing code and business authority.
beats.camera_or_motion: Static camera; frame-driven focus, strike, and type replacement. The center authority axis begins before the next beat.
beats.asset_provenance: Owned deterministic typography and motion in AuthorityBoundaryConceptPrototype.tsx, bounded by fact-authority-framework.
beats.sound_cue: Approved narration only; no music or sound effects.
beats.transition_out: The center authority axis remains while the opening hierarchy clears and the low-risk statement enters.
beats.fallback: One static porcelain-and-indigo image-sequence plate carrying the question and the writing-code-versus-authority distinction.

beats.entry_visual: The inherited authority axis and its marker are already visible beneath ‘Move fast where failure is cheap.’
beats.visual_reason: A short calm hold preserves the legitimate fast lane before the argument introduces higher-authority work.
beats.camera_or_motion: Static camera; the shared marker holds near DISPOSABLE while the low-risk statement settles and clears.
beats.asset_provenance: Owned deterministic typography and shared-axis motion in AuthorityBoundaryConceptPrototype.tsx, derived from Aaron’s authority framework.

beats.entry_visual: The low-risk axis persists as its marker begins moving toward CRITICAL SYSTEM and SYSTEM OF RECORD.
beats.visual_reason: One spatial continuum makes authority, rather than authorship or code size, the variable that changes the review decision.
beats.camera_or_motion: Static camera; the marker travels along one axis, authoritative labels enter, and a small ledger appears only with ‘system of record’ using a 12-frame fade and 10-pixel settle. It does not rotate, bounce, loop, or recur. ‘Who wrote it?’ then yields to ‘What is this code allowed to change?’

The exact prompt and QA are in imgs/video/sprites/authority-ledger-v1-manifest.json. It is an illustrative mnemonic, not evidence, a real interface, or an incident artifact.
